name: MCP3204-CI_ST
title: MCP3204 / MCP3208: 4- and 8-channel 12-bit SAR ADCs with SPI interface, 2.7 V to 5.5 V
summary: A pair of 12-bit successive-approximation converters with a built-in sample-and-hold and an input multiplexer: the MCP3204 has four inputs and the MCP3208 eight, usable one by one against ground or as pseudo-differential pairs (two pairs on the MCP3204, four on the MCP3208). Each conversion is commanded over a four-wire SPI-compatible port (modes 0,0 and 1,1) that also carries the result back. A single 2.7 V to 5.5 V supply runs the part and a separate VREF pin sets the span; the rate reaches 100 ksps at 5 V and 50 ksps at 2.7 V. The B grade holds INL to ±1 LSB and the C grade to ±2 LSB; DNL is ±1 LSB in both.

circuits.title: Second-order anti-aliasing filter driving the MCP3204
circuits.description: An MCP601 op amp wired as a second-order Sallen-Key low-pass (R1, R2, C1, C2), its gain set by R4 and R3, buffers and band-limits the signal into the MCP3204's IN+ input; IN- is tied to ground. An MCP1541 provides a 4.096 V reference to VREF, decoupled by 1 µF, with 0.1 µF on its input. VDD is decoupled by 10 µF and 1 µF.

operation.text: A conventional successive-approximation converter. The input is held on an on-chip sampling capacitor, which tracks it for 1.5 clocks beginning at the fourth rising CLK edge after the start bit; the held charge is then turned into a 12-bit result, one bit per clock. Rates up to 100 ksps are reachable.

Each conversion's command picks single-ended or pseudo-differential use. In pseudo-differential mode one channel of a pair (CH0/CH1, CH2/CH3 and so on) is IN+ and the other IN-; IN- may sit only ±100 mV from VSS and rejects small common-mode noise present on both. If IN- sits over 1 LSB under VSS, reaching 000h needs IN+ under VSS; if IN- sits over 1 LSB over VSS, reaching FFFh needs IN+ over VREF.

Each input pad presents about 7 pF of pin capacitance, ±1 nA of junction leakage and clamp junctions (VT = 0.6 V) to VDD and VSS; behind it a sampling switch of about 1 kΩ feeds the 20 pF DAC capacitance. The source resistance adds to the switch resistance and lengthens the time needed to charge the capacitor to 12-bit accuracy inside the 1.5-cycle window, so a higher source impedance raises offset, gain and INL error. The graph of maximum clock frequency against source resistance gives the clock that keeps the INL shift under 0.1 LSB.

VREF sets the analog input span; lowering it shrinks the LSB in proportion. Any instability of an external reference shows up directly in the conversions, and the reference's own layout guidance applies. While the LSB-first copy or the trailing zeros are being clocked out, VREF goes high impedance.

A transaction begins when CS/SHDN falls; a part powered up with CS/SHDN low needs it taken high and low again first. The first clock with CS/SHDN low and DIN high is the start bit, followed by SGL/DIFF and D2, D1, D0 for the channel. Sampling begins with the fourth rising edge after the start bit and ends when the fifth clock after it falls; DIN is ignored for the clock after D0. On the next falling edge DOUT gives a low null bit, then B11 to B0, MSB first, each changing on a falling edge. More clocks with CS/SHDN still low return the result again LSB first (B1 to B11), and after that zeros for as long as clocking continues. While that tail is clocked out the bias circuit and comparator are powered down. Leading zeros may be clocked in on DIN before the start bit.

With a port that moves 8 bits at a time, sending data on falling edges and latching on rising edges, three bytes make one conversion. The first byte is five zeros, the start bit, SGL/DIFF and D2; the second begins with D1 and D0, the rest ignored. The byte received during the second transfer holds three undefined bits, the null bit and B11 to B8; the third holds B7 to B0. The MSB appears on DOUT when clock 12 falls. Mode 0,0 (clock idle low) and mode 1,1 (clock idle high) both work this way.

Charge leaks from the sampling capacitor during the conversion, so the time from sample end to the last of the 12 data bits must stay within 1.2 ms (an effective clock of 10 kHz); at 85°C, the worst case, the charge holds for at least that long. A slower conversion can add linearity error beyond the ratings. Neither a constant clock rate nor a set duty cycle is needed, provided every timing limit is kept.

A source that is not low impedance needs a buffer, or conversions lose accuracy. A low-pass anti-aliasing filter ahead of the input removes signals that would fold back into the band; the antialias-filter circuit uses an op amp for both jobs.

Bypass VDD with 1 µF placed as close to the pin as possible. Keep digital and analog traces well apart, with no traces under the part or its bypass capacitor, and keep fast lines such as the clock far from analog traces. An analog ground plane holds every device at the same ground potential, and running VDD to each device in a star from one point cuts errors from shared return currents.

AGND serves the analog side (sample capacitor, capacitor array, comparator) and DGND the digital side (SPI interface, shift register, control logic); inside, the two join through the substrate at 5 Ω to 10 Ω. Without a ground plane both pins join board VSS; with a plane, or with separate analog and digital planes, both pins join the analog plane. The VDD pin is bypassed to that plane with 0.1 µF.
